verdicts.reason: Two tests jointly exercise all three named failure modes with real assertions: 'rejects import and missing entrypoint input' covers import/undefined/unresolvable-path cases; 'rejects a dangling symlink without throwing' creates a real dangling symlink and confirms false without an uncaught exception. Inspected isDirectExecution's implementation: the only path to false for a truthy, non-matching argvEntry is the catch block after realpathSync throws, confirming the catch path (not just the early return) is genuinely exercised by the dangling-symlink case.

The 'module import alone does not execute the CLI' test spawns a subprocess that only imports the module and asserts empty stdout/stderr and exit 0. Independently confirmed process.argv has no argv[1] under this exact node --input-type=module --eval import shape (so isDirectExecution's early !argvEntry return prevents main), and confirmed via direct invocation that if main() ran it would print several KB of help text, so the empty-stdout pass is real evidence of non-execution, not a superficial check.

Ran node --test test/bin-entrypoint.test.js; the 'version executes identically through the real entrypoint and a symlink' test spawns the real bin/vibepro.js with argv ['version'] and a freshly created file symlink to it with the same argv via spawnSync, asserting matching exit code 0 and matching stdout content. This is a genuine black-box process-level check that actually invokes the version subcommand through both paths, not a string/field existence check.
